blocks.html:
The recommendation

Three things, in the order we'd do them. Nothing here is a rebuild from scratch: your flows work, they just stop early and one of them is pointed at the wrong list.

  1. Double the campaigns, 4 a month to 8. $300 each, so $1,200 a month more. Your own weeks say it's worth $97,679 to $195,358 a year.
  2. Add 8 emails to the automations you already have, and fix the welcome trigger. A one-off $2,400. Worth about $100,459 a year, then it runs for nothing.
  3. Rebuild the sign-up form, then keep testing it. $500 a month. At 0.49% it is the cheapest number in the account to move, and moving it to 1.0% is worth $21,566 a year.

1. Your campaigns are under-sent

Over 52 weeks, May ’25 to Oct ’26, you sent one campaign in 40 ordinary weeks and two in 5. The one-send weeks earned $6,494. The two-send weeks earned $10,564. The second send earns a little less on its own ($5,282 against $6,494), so there is some overlap, but it adds 81% of a campaign rather than splitting one in half.

You will see more unsubscribes. That is the trade and it is worth naming, because the rate and the count move in opposite directions. The rate per send falls, 0.29% to 0.22%, but a two-send week loses about 66 people where a one-send week loses 38. Across 48 extra campaigns that is roughly 1,300 more unsubscribes a year. The extra send brings $4,070 a week and costs 28 of them, so you are trading one unsubscribe for about $148 of revenue. Black Friday week Nov ’25 is the same at full stretch: 5 campaigns, $35,727, 127 unsubscribes against a normal week's 38, and still the lowest rate on the board at 0.19%.

blocks.html:
2. Your automations stop too early, and one is misrouted

You run 4 flows and they are good flows. The problem is where they end, and who they reach.

The welcome is pointed at one of your two sign-up lists. It fires when somebody joins Master List, which took 472 people this year. 992 more joined Newsletter and got nothing. That is the single cheapest fix in this document, because that flow earns $32 for every email it sends, more than any other flow you run. Pointing it at both lists is worth $35,941 a year on its own, before a single new email is written.

Your post-purchase flow ends on day 16. The one called Onboarding is really your post-purchase series: it fires on an order, sends 5 emails, and then stops. Meanwhile 6,856 people bought from you last year and placed 7,408 orders, so only 552 were repeat buys on a $737 average order. The second, third and fourth purchase all happen after day 16, and nothing of yours is there.

So the 8 emails go where the money already is: 3 more on the welcome, 3 after the purchase window closes, and 2 on the abandoned cart, which earns $29 an email and is your second best.

3. The sign-up form is the cheapest number in the account to move

289,986 people saw your sign-up form in the last 12 months. 1,424 filled it in. That is 0.49%, where two to four percent is ordinary. Everything else in this proposal works on the people you already have. This is the only line that adds more of them.

We'd rebuild it once and then keep testing it, month after month: offer, timing, wording, mobile against desktop. Getting from 0.49% to 1.0% is roughly 1,476 extra subscribers a year. At half what a subscriber is worth to you today ($29 a year across 27,372 profiles), that is $21,566. It is also the only part of this that gets better the longer it runs.

What it costs and what it returns

48 extra campaigns a year at $300$14,400 · $1,200/mo
8 flow emails at $300, built once$2,400 · one-off
Sign-up testing at $500 a month$6,000 · $500/mo
Year one$22,800
Campaigns, at half your evidenced rate$97,679
Welcome pointed at both lists$35,941
8 added emails$64,518
Sign-up form at 1.0%$21,566
Year one$219,704
Return on the spend9.6× to 13.9×

For scale: the 46 campaigns you ran in the last 12 months cost $13,800 and are credited with $306,783, which is 22 times the fee. None of this needs a new result. It needs the ones you already get, more often and from more people.

What doing nothing costs, and what doing half of it costs

Your list is already shrinking. 1,311 people joined in the last 12 months and 1,770 left, a net loss of 459. Campaigns earn money from the list you have. They do not build it, and at 8 a month they spend it faster: add the 1,300 extra unsubscribes above and the net loss is nearer 1,759 a year.

That is why the three parts belong together. The campaigns earn more from the list, the flows earn more from each person on it, and the sign-up form is the only thing that refills it. Take the first on its own and you are spending an asset faster without topping it up. You are also at 27,372 of your 28,000 Klaviyo profiles, so the people you keep need to be worth more, not just more numerous.

What it asks of your team

  • Nothing for the flows. We write them, you approve them once, they run by themselves from then on.
  • No new approvals process for the campaigns. Same monthly batch, twice the emails in it.
  • Nothing for the testing. It happens on your site, we report what won, you never have to look at it unless you want to.
  • No commitment to fill the calendar. 8 is a ceiling we're allowed to use, not a quota. If revenue per campaign or unsubscribes move the wrong way we drop back, and you've learned where your ceiling is.

Campaigns. 52 weeks of your own sends, May ’25 to Oct ’26, grouped by how many went out that week. 7 offer weeks and 3 peak weeks are excluded, so it is ordinary week against ordinary week and a sale can't inflate the step. A cadence is only quoted where you ran it at least three times.

The unsubscribe count. Your two-send weeks also went to a slightly wider audience per send (15,573 against 13,884), so part of the extra 28 is reach rather than frequency. We have left it all in the frequency column, which makes 1,300 a year the pessimistic reading.

The added emails. Each one is priced at a quarter of what the flow it joins already earns per email: half because last-click attribution is generous, half again because the sixth email in a series never performs like the first. Pointing the welcome at both lists is priced at half rather than a quarter, because those emails are already written and already performing; they are simply not being sent to everyone. Every volume is discounted 25% for people who buy, leave or drop out of a series part way.

The form. Views and submissions are Klaviyo form events for the 12 months to 31 Oct 2026. A subscriber is valued at the $29 a year your email programme earns per active profile, then halved. Order, customer and list figures are Klaviyo events over the same window, read from your account when this page was built.

Revenue is Klaviyo's attribution on last click, the generous reading rather than the strict one. That is why everything here is quoted at half or less, and the case still stands there. A holdout test gives you the strict number and we will run one if you want it.

reports.summary: Send more, finish the automations you already have, and fix a sign-up form converting at 0.49%. $22,800 in year one against $219,704, every figure taken at half of what your account already earns or less.
